faqs.q: When should Bradenton snowbirds have their home sealed?

faqs.q: Rats are in our Palmetto packing shed — what does your work cover?
faqs.a: The structure and the trapping: we seal dock doors, vents, and conduit entries with gnaw-proof material, trap the resident population with nonchemical methods checked daily, and set the food-discipline rules — produce waste contained, pallets off walls, spills cleaned — that keep the building from refilling. faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Lakewood Ranch?

faqs.q: Alligators are in our Lakewood Ranch pond — who is responsible?
faqs.a: FWC's nuisance alligator program is the only remover: alligators four feet or longer posing a threat to people, pets, or property get a contracted state trapper through that program, and neither the HOA nor any private company may substitute. Most Ranch pond gators are under the threshold and simply resident — keep pets leashed away from dawn and dusk banks, never feed, and report bold behavior. Our role stops at honest identification and the referral; anyone offering pond gator removal for hire is offering something Florida law does not sell.

faqs.q: Raccoons raid our Anna Maria rental's trash every week — what fixes it?
faqs.a: The enclosure, not the raccoon population. Island raccoons are expert and permanent; an unlatched can is a standing reservation. Locking, raccoon-proof enclosures — the island's better rentals all use them — plus no food waste left outdoors after turnover cleanings ends the raids within a week or two. If raccoons have graduated to the attic, that is our removal-and-seal work; but trash raiding alone is an equipment answer, and we would rather sell you the truth than a trapping contract.

Cottage craft is the service here: small roofs, older materials, rental turnover. We seal with salt-rated materials and document for off-island owners with photos as standard. Turtle and shorebird questions are referred to the island's monitors and FWC, proudly.

faqs.q: Moles are ruining our Ellenton lawn — how do you treat them?
faqs.a: By trapping the tunnels that are active now, not poisoning the whole yard. Eastern moles tunnel for earthworms and grubs; we probe for the main travel runs — the straight, surface ridges between deeper systems — set traps in those runs, and check them daily. Chemical grub treatments belong to lawn and pest licensees and rarely end moles anyway, since earthworms are the staple. Expect a short program of sets and checks, quoted by yard scope after we walk the tunnel map with you.

Ellenton service mixes eras like the town does: plantation-era landscape questions (a tortoise under the live oaks is a referral and a photo opportunity), mid-century home sealing, and newer-subdivision gap audits east of the interstate.
